reason: The target is the Study 1 one-factor between-subjects omnibus MANOVA comparing the three mutually exclusive LPA groups (n = 175, 30, 22; N = 227) across the 11 LPA indicator variables on PDF page 8 (printed page 6). Because this is a single-factor between-subjects MANOVA without covariates or additional factors, no other effects are partialled out and multivariate eta-squared and partial eta-squared are identical: from Wilks's lambda = 0.67 with k = 3 groups and p = 11 variables (s = min(p, k - 1) = 2), partial eta-squared is 1 - 0.67^(1/2) = 0.1815, matching the printed .18 (0.18).
